text:
ops-bot: [CRITICAL] region=mia1 control-plane heartbeat missing for 2 consecutive checks — all region controllers reporting 'silence'. https://mon.redwood/alert/ABCD1234 :rotating_light:
jamal: i'm getting paged, jumping in. seeing 5xxs from mia1 edge nodes in the last 90s.
maria: metrics -> controlplane_api_latency spike to 4s then timeouts. controlplane leader flapping.
ken: GKE-style provider? or our private k8s? we still have k8s events showing frequent leader-election.
ryan_sre: this looks like a network fabric issue between control-plane and nodeagent. node heartbeats dropped. kube-apiserver still up on masters but etcd quorums unstable.
jamal: running quick checks: ```kubectl get nodes --context=mia1 -o wide
NAME             STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-node-001     NotReady   worker   12d  v1.27.3
gpu-node-002     NotReady   worker   9d   v1.27.3
master-0         Ready      master   30d  v1.27.3
master-1         NotReady   master   30d  v1.27.3
```
maria: logs from node-agent show repeated TLS handshake timeouts to controlplane IPs.
ken: can we reach nodes from controlplane? `ssh master-0` -> `curl http://10.10.1.5:10250/healthz` ?
jamal: tried that, connection reset. packet loss on the fabric between masters and worker-subnet.
ryan_sre: sounds like a routing churn in provider network or our VPC route propagation feed. check BGP/route tables.
elaine: initiating incident call in #incident-mia1 now. tagging oncall. @oncall-bot please escalate to P1 and create incident doc.
oncall-bot: Incident P1 created: INC-2026-039-MIA1. Join retrospective -> https://wiki.redwood/incidents/INC-2026-039-MIA1
maria: customer-facing impact: ~18% of requests hitting mia1 returning 502/504; most of internal traffic OK because of multi-region routing but some clients pinned to mia1.
ken: mitigation plan: 1) stop new allocations to mia1 via router policy, 2) shift edge traffic to primary fallback us-east1, 3) spin emergency Dedicated burst in us-east1 for GPU-heavy workloads.
jamal: on it. updating router policy:```POST /v1/traffic-routes/update {
  "region_action": {"mia1": "drain", "us-east1": "accept"}
}```
maria: confirm — draining means no new sessions, existing sessions continue for short TTL (30s). good.
ken: we also need to set model fallback for short requests -> change route to cpu-quantized variant in us-east1 for background jobs to reduce GPU capacity pressure.
ryan_sre: capacity note: us-east1 Dedicated has 120 GPU slots free. expected additional demand if we shift. if we burst with cloud-burst, cost est ~ $12k/day. confirm finance ok?
elaine: short term priority is availability. bill later. :+1:
jamal: executed router update — `200 OK` rolling out. starting traffic switch, watch ingress metrics.
maria: ingress mia1 qps down 70% within 45s, errors dropping in edge -> us-east1 qps up correspondingly. good.
ken: triggering autoscale for us-east1 dedicated pool to add 24 GPUs: `POST /internal/dedicated/scale?region=us-east1&add=24`
jamal: scale request accepted, nodes provisioning. time to allocate ~7m.
ryan_sre: provisioning logs show cloud provider returning rate-limit errors for some images; retrying with staggered backoff.
elaine: ops, please prepare a short status update for status.redwood.com: summarize impacted region, mitigation (traffic shifted to us-east1, draining mia1), ETA for next update 15m.
jamal: drafted status: "Customers previously routed to MIA1 may see intermittent 5xx errors. Traffic has been shifted to US-EAST1 while we investigate a control-plane network partition in MIA1. Engineering is provisioning additional capacity. We will post updates every 15 minutes."
oncall-bot: Status page updated.
maria: immediate ask: do we want to failover persistent storage? any writes pinned to mia1?
ken: our S3 layer is global, but etcd for cluster is local. workloads that need local etcd (stateful sets with local PV) may have issues. we should mark some workloads as degraded.
ryan_sre: i'll run quick job to identify stateful pods pinned to mia1 and try to mark as read-only where safe.
j amal: running: `kubectl get pods -n prod -o jsonpath='{range .items[?(@.spec.nodeName=="gpu-node-001")]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}'` -> few critical pods (model-serving-v2-5), shifting them will require model warmup.
elaine: decision board: 1) keep mia1 drained, 2) redirect all new traffic to us-east1, 3) provision burst GPUs in us-east1, 4) open vendor ticket with provider for network fabric analysis. assigned: jamal (traffic), ryan_sre (stateful check), ken (capacity), maria (customer comms), elaine (incident lead).
ken: vendor ticket created: TKT-9981 -> awaiting provider network triage.
maria: I've posted to #customer-ops with guidance for customers pinned to mia1 and included mitigation steps.
ryan_sre: collecting pcap and controlplane logs for postmortem: `/var/log/controlplane/etcd.log`, `/var/log/agent/agent.log` archived to s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-039-MIA1/
jamal: ingress error rate back to baseline after shift. keeping mia1 drained and monitoring for 30m.
elaine: good work team. next update in 15m or earlier if provider reports root cause. starting timeline doc now.
oncall-bot: next update scheduled at 2312346078."
